statement: The function returns a result r and r = max { C(j) | 0 <= j < len(conflictingPairs) }, where for each j, C(j) is the number of integer intervals [L,R] with 1 <= L <= R <= n such that for every i with 0 <= i < len(conflictingPairs) and i != j, it is not the case that both L <= conflictingPairs[i][0] <= R and L <= conflictingPairs[i][1] <= R. Equivalently, C(j) is the number of non-empty contiguous subarrays of nums=[1,2,...,n] that contain both endpoints of no remaining conflicting pair after deleting the single occurrence at index j.
preconditions: n is an integer with 2 <= n <= 100000. conflictingPairs is a slice of vectors of I64. len(conflictingPairs) is between 1 and 2*n inclusive. For every i with 0 <= i < len(conflictingPairs), conflictingPairs[i] has length 2, and its two entries are integers a_i,b_i with 1 <= a_i <= n, 1 <= b_i <= n, and a_i != b_i. The pairs are not assumed distinct and no ordering of them is assumed.
